name: quality-v1
purpose: Before/after evaluation for the answer-quality milestone (dates, follow-up grouping, joins, zero counts, capability replies, unavailable data). References were written before any model output was seen. Never add these questions or reference queries to knowledge_base/.
reference_time_note: All data is from 2023, so a 2024 reference date separates correct year-aware ranges from MONTH()-only filters. The evaluation pins both the prompt date and MySQL's session timestamp to this time.
split_note: dev items may guide prompt and knowledge changes; heldout items are only run for the baseline and the final comparison and must not be used for tuning.

turns: How many appointments are there this month?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE appointment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND appointment_date < '2024-02-01'

scenarios.notes: Correct answer is 0 (January 2024). MONTH(appointment_date) = MONTH(CURDATE()) without the year returns 20 (January 2023).

turns: What was the total billed amount last month?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM billing WHERE bill_date >= '2023-12-01' AND bill_date < '2024-01-01'

scenarios.notes: Last month of 2024-01-15 is December 2023. MONTH(CURDATE()) - 1 gives month 0 and YEAR(CURDATE()) gives 2024: both return NULL/0.

turns: How many treatments were performed in March 2023?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM treatments WHERE treatment_date >= '2023-03-01' AND treatment_date < '2023-04-01'

turns: How many appointments took place in the second quarter of 2023?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE appointment_date >= '2023-04-01' AND appointment_date < '2023-07-01'

scenarios.notes: Must include 30 June; an end bound of '2023-06-30' with < would drop it.

turns: How many bills were issued from 15 March 2023 to 15 April 2023, including both days?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing WHERE bill_date BETWEEN '2023-03-15' AND '2023-04-15'

turns: Show the number of appointments in each month of 2023, in calendar order.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(appointment_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE appointment_date >= '2023-01-01' AND appointment_date < '2024-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(appointment_date, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month
alternative_reference_sqls: SELECT MONTH(appointment_date), COUNT(*) FROM appointments WHERE YEAR(appointment_date) = 2023 GROUP BY MONTH(appointment_date) ORDER BY MONTH(appointment_date)

turns: Which patients registered last year?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT patient_id, first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE registration_date >= '2023-01-01' AND registration_date < '2024-01-01'

turns: What is the total billed amount for each doctor specialization?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.specialization, SUM(b.amount) FROM billing AS b JOIN treatments AS t ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id GROUP BY d.specialization

turns: For patients insured by MedCare Plus, how many treatments of each treatment type did they receive?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT t.treatment_type, COUNT(*) FROM treatments AS t JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN patients AS p ON a.patient_id = p.patient_id WHERE p.insurance_provider = 'MedCare Plus' GROUP BY t.treatment_type

turns: What is the total amount of failed bills in each hospital branch?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.hospital_branch, SUM(b.amount) FROM billing AS b JOIN treatments AS t ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id WHERE b.payment_status = 'Failed' GROUP BY d.hospital_branch

turns: How many appointments has each patient had? Include patients who have none.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT p.patient_id, COUNT(a.appointment_id) FROM patients AS p LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.patient_id = p.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id

scenarios.notes: Two patients have no appointments, so an inner join returns 48 rows instead of 50.

turns: How many emergency appointments does each doctor have, including doctors with none?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.doctor_id, COUNT(a.appointment_id) FROM doctors AS d LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id AND a.reason_for_visit = 'Emergency' GROUP BY d.doctor_id

turns: Which insurance providers cover more than 16 patients?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT insurance_provider FROM patients GROUP BY insurance_provider HAVING COUNT(*) > 16

scenarios.notes: Counts are 18, 16, 10, 6: '>= 16' would wrongly include WellnessCorp.

turns: How many different patients have at least one bill?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM billing

turns: What is the average treatment cost for each treatment type, rounded to 2 decimals?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT treatment_type, ROUND(AVG(cost), 2) FROM treatments GROUP BY treatment_type

turns: How many completed appointments does each doctor have?
Do it by hospital branch

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.hospital_branch, COUNT(*) FROM appointments AS a JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY d.hospital_branch

scenarios.notes: Replacement: the doctor grouping is dropped, the completed filter is kept.

turns: What is the total billed amount per doctor?
Show it per specialization instead

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.specialization, SUM(b.amount) FROM billing AS b JOIN treatments AS t ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id GROUP BY d.specialization

turns: How many appointments are there for each status?
Also break it down by hospital branch

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.status, d.hospital_branch, COUNT(*) FROM appointments AS a JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id GROUP BY a.status, d.hospital_branch

scenarios.notes: Additive: both status and branch remain groupings.

turns: What is the total amount of paid bills for each payment method?
Split that by patient gender as well

expect.reference_sql: SELECT b.payment_method, p.gender, SUM(b.amount) FROM billing AS b JOIN patients AS p ON b.patient_id = p.patient_id WHERE b.payment_status = 'Paid' GROUP BY b.payment_method, p.gender

turns: How many appointments does each doctor have, including doctors with no appointments?
Only no-shows

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.doctor_id, COUNT(a.appointment_id) FROM doctors AS d LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id AND a.status = 'No-show' GROUP BY d.doctor_id

turns: How many cancelled appointments are there?
What about the other status?
scenarios.notes: There are three other statuses, so the follow-up is genuinely ambiguous.

turns: How many completed appointments does each doctor have?
How many patients use each insurance provider?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT insurance_provider, COUNT(*) FROM patients GROUP BY insurance_provider

turns: How many patients are female?
What is the capital of France?
How many bills were issued in January 2023?
What about the previous month?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM billing WHERE bill_date >= '2022-12-01' AND bill_date < '2023-01-01'

scenarios.notes: The previous month is December 2022 (0 bills); December 2023 (12 bills) is the year-boundary mistake.

turns: On what date was each paid bill actually paid?
scenarios.notes: There is no payment date. The answer must say so and ask whether bill_date is acceptable, not silently use it.

turns: How many bills were paid during March 2023?
scenarios.notes: 'Paid during March' asks when payment happened; only the bill date exists.

turns: What diagnosis did each patient receive?
scenarios.notes: No diagnosis column. Any outcome that runs no SQL (cannot answer or clarification) is acceptable.
